id.description: Citation marker as it appears in the paper (e.g. '1', '12', 'Smith2020')

relation.description: How this reference relates to the citing paper, judged from in-text citation context.

roles.description: Functional roles this reference plays for the citing paper; one or more. background=field/concept context; motivation=why the problem matters or a prior limitation that motivates this work; uses_method=a method/architecture/algorithm/technique/tool/optimizer/library reused or built upon; uses_data=a dataset or benchmark used; extends=the direct predecessor this paper improves on; baseline=compared against experimentally; contrast=disagreed with or critiqued; future_work=cited only as a future direction; related=passing mention. Use 'related' only when no stronger role fits.

stance.description: How the citing paper positions itself: builds on it (supportive), neutral mention, or critiques/contrasts it (critical). Default neutral when unclear.

salience.description: central = load-bearing for this paper's argument or experiments (a main baseline, a core building block, or relied on repeatedly); peripheral = passing mention.

provides_name.description: For uses_method/uses_data/extends/baseline roles, the single most specific named artifact the citing paper takes from this work (e.g. 'Transformer', 'ImageNet', 'Adam', 'BERT'). Empty string for background/related/future_work or when no concrete artifact is named.

provides_unit_ids.description: Always output an empty array []. Links to spine unit IDs are filled deterministically by the pipeline after section extraction; never populate this yourself.
